body:
# Independent root audit of candidate 0f025bdf9a51573b

The root read the complete proof independently on 2026-09-09. The argument
proves an auxiliary continuous theorem and does not prove OC.

- The radial quantile calculation is correct. From
  t=(lambda/r+(1-lambda)/s)^(-1), a=lambda t/r, b=(1-lambda)t/s,
  one obtains a+b=1, t=ar+bs, and
  t^(p-1)t'=t^p[a/(r^p f_1)+b/(s^p f_2)]. Weighted AM--GM, followed by
  log-concavity and t>=r^a s^b, yields the stated lower bound one. It
  requires only p>0 and positivity on the ray interiors, not a mode at zero.
- Ray endpoints cause no missing mass: both quantiles are differentiable on
  (0,1), the harmonic radius is strictly increasing, and its image starts
  at zero. Integrating first on compact subintervals and then increasing
  to (0,1) justifies the improper change of variables.
- Integrability and an interior positive ball bound the density globally
  by integrating the midpoint inequality over a translated half-size ball.
  The positive superlevel set containing that ball must be bounded. Its
  radial comparison supplies a uniform exponential tail, which also gives
  continuity of the radial integral by dominated convergence.
- Boundary-to-boundary convexity, together with radial homogeneity and
  inclusion of zero, does imply convexity of the entire radial body. The
  uniform radial bounds supply compactness and nonempty interior.
- Joint cap-mass continuity follows because each limiting boundary
  hyperplane has zero density measure. Depth tends to zero at infinity
  and is uniformly positive at an interior point. Hence its maximum is
  attained at a point strictly inside the support.
- If active normals admit a strict separating direction, moving the
  center in the opposite direction gains a slab of uniformly positive
  density for every nearby active normal. The compact complement has a
  positive old gap. This proves the balancing certificate without assuming
  differentiability of the density or uniqueness of the center.
- The radial body preserves every through-center cap mass, has volume one,
  and the finite balanced active normals cover every possible competing
  center by a cap of mass at most alpha. Thus optimality, not merely depth
  at one point, is preserved. Applying ordinary continuous Grunbaum here
  is not circular with OC.
- The argument includes r=1. All measures in this auxiliary theorem are
  absolutely continuous; their boundary hyperplanes are null for that
  stated reason. No conclusion for singular target laws is inferred.
- For exp(-p_T) with a centered simplex T, level sets are dilates of T and
  affine vertex permutations preserve the law. Quasiconcavity of depth
  makes the permutation average zero deepest. The claimed sharpness is
  valid.

No mathematical gap was found in this audit. A suitable log-concave law
in a mixed-integer fiber, with the required simultaneous halfspace
domination, has not been constructed in general.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
